preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10⁴) representing the number of test cases.
Each of the next 4t lines contains exactly two integers x and y (0 ≤ x, y ≤ 10⁹) representing coordinates of a point.

preconditions.expression: all(all(int(x) == int(x) and int(y) == int(y) for x, y in [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[i:i+4]]) for i in range(1, 4*t+1, 4))
preconditions.description: All coordinates in each test case are integers within the bounds 0 ≤ x, y ≤ 10⁹.

preconditions.expression: all(len(set((int(x), int(y)) for x, y in [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[i:i+4]])) == 4 for i in range(1, 4*t+1, 4))
preconditions.description: All four points in each test case are distinct.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().split() == [str(min_steps) for min_steps in [compute_min_steps(points) for points in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[i:i+4]] for i in range(1, 4*t+1, 4)]]
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is a single integer representing the minimum number of steps required to move the four points to form an axis-aligned square (including side length 0).

postconditions.expression: all(min_steps >= 0 for min_steps in [compute_min_steps(points) for points in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[i:i+4]] for i in range(1, 4*t+1, 4)]])
postconditions.description: The minimum number of steps is always a non-negative integer.
